rules.repetition_runs: phrase reproduced at least as often in the second pass -> unresolved (could be genuine); not reproduced and second pass clean -> resolved-by-second-pass; otherwise unresolved
rules.high_temperature_segments: ratio >= threshold and second pass clean -> resolved-by-second-pass; otherwise unresolved; segments inside a repetition run inherit the run status

parahas tasmātu bhāvo anyo avyatto avyattāt sanātanaḥ
yahaḥ sarveṣu bhūteṣu naśyatsu na vinaśyati
Tasmādh paraha means beyond that Saguna Avyatta.
There is another Avyatta which is called the Sanātana Avyatta.
yahaḥ sarveṣu bhūteṣu naśyatsu na vinaśyati
naśyatsu means when they are perish.
The Brahmans realm and the lower realms.
Indicative that by saying satyam jnanam anandam brahma.
A meditating on this verse until the two avyattas are clearly distinguished and the nirguna avyatta stand in the same position,
Sankaracharya now identifies the two avyattas as the same.
Whereas, the nirguna avyatta which is in the night, ratri agame or the mahapralaya, it dissolves.
The sambandha between the two is called kārya-kāraṇa within māyā but as ādiṣṭhāna.
maya kārana and the nirguna paramatman.
Na vinas yati is a paramartha pramana or Avyakta, Nirguna Avyakta.
Yaha avyaktaha akshara ityuktas tam vedanta vitha paramam gatim ahu.
Yam gattuayam prapyana nivartande tadparamamdama mama.
in a single verse four threads have been tied to the mind
The Briharadayaranya Upanishad says Etadvaitad Aksharam Gargi.
Na punar na nivartande tad dhama paramam mama.
The equation, tad dhama paramam mama, mama swaroopam, param brahma, krishna's param brahma, is not a loka or krishna inhibits, but a loka.

It is krishna's own swaroopa, which is the paramam brahman, which is akshara, which is also abhyakta, which he mentioned that adi yajnam atradehe, which is the witness present in all of us as the knower of everything.
Om Shanti Shanti Shanti Hari Om Shri Gurubhyo Namaha Hari Om
